titleStmt.title: The neural correlates of consciousness: new experimental approaches needed?
titleStmt.author: Hohwy

publicationStmt.p: Tag layer of the DHSS Meta-Tagging Project. The article text is reproduced from the staged copy named in sourceDesc and is not altered; the tags are held separately in standOff so that overlapping and nested spans are preserved.

bibl.title: The neural correlates of consciousness: new experimental approaches needed?

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: critique
span.quote: Methodological and conceptual considerations of a number of concrete studies show that both approaches are problematic: the content-based approach seems to set aside crucial aspects of consciousness; and the state-based approach seems over-inclusive in a way that is hard to rectify without losing sight of the crucial conscious–unconscious contrast.

span.label: neural correlates of consciousness
span.quote: Finding the neural correlates of consciousness (the NCC) is a major focus of cognitive neuroscience.

span.label: conceptual-analysis
span.quote: It is shown here that, from the point of view of philosophy of science, these approaches are problematic both conceptually and methodologically.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Relegating state consciousness to a background condition screens off any contribution the state NCC makes to constituting a content's being conscious, so the design can only speak to which content is represented
span.quote: The basic issue is that, by focusing on the first contrast, any contribution from the neural correlates of state consciousness to the constitution of a content’s being conscious is effectively screened off.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: The pre-existing conscious state, not the induced content, may be the actual difference-maker that renders the content conscious
span.quote: The preexisting conscious state could very well be the difference-maker for the content’s being conscious.

span.label: The argument shows the current paradigms need re-development, not that no NCC can ever be found.
span.quote: Though the present arguments by no means show that an NCC can never be found, they do show that the current paradigms are in need of re-evaluation and re-development in the light of methodological and conceptual considerations.

span.label: The paper is neutral between theories of consciousness and does not adjudicate them.
span.quote: The arguments presented here are neutral on these theories but do indeed suggest that the current NCC methodologies taken separately most likely cannot gain much direct evidence for or against them.

span.label: The design is argued to be flawed in the way a carcinogen study would be if every mouse already had the cancer: the property of interest is presupposed in every subject.
span.quote: In the carcinogen case, the researcher’s study design is flawed because she is interested in the property of being a certain kind of cancer, which is the very property whose instantiation is presupposed in all the mice

span.label: On the author's own account the approach can at best deliver the conditions for a content being SELECTED for consciousness, which is a different question from a content being conscious.
span.quote: At best, I now say, it will find the minimally sufficient conditions for selection into consciousness

span.label: Tightening the experimental control defeats the aim: the better the content is matched, the harder the conscious/unconscious contrast is to sustain.
span.quote: as content is more carefully matched, it becomes harder to uphold the contrast between conscious and unconscious states, which is crucial for the state-based approach

span.label: The field states that absence of the neural marker cannot be read as absence of the phenomenon.
span.quote: The researchers in this field of study are also very clear that the absence of thalamocortical activity, or of SMA activity in response to requests to imagine tennis, cannot be taken as evidence of absence of consciousness

span.label: A CONTROL GROUP ARGUED AWAY RATHER THAN OMITTED. Owen's case that the vegetative-state patient's sustained SMA response is voluntary rests on its duration and on its changing to order - and the author notes that this logic, if it works, makes a control group unnecessary, since ANY brain activity time-locked to the requests would show the same thing. He calls that consequence puzzling rather than wrong.
span.quote: it is slightly puzzling that this logic removes the need for comparison with a control group: consideration solely of the VS patient’s SMA activity is enough since any pattern of activity anywhere in the brain that is time-locked to the requests could demonstrate the voluntariness.

span.label: neural correlates of consciousness
span.quote: Finding the neural correlates of consciousness (the NCC) is a major focus of cognitive neuroscience

span.label: content consciousness
span.quote: the minimally sufficient neural conditions for a specific (mostly representational) content being conscious rather than not being conscious

span.label: state consciousness
span.quote: notice that Searle uses the term ‘‘unified conscious field” as a cognate term for state of consciousness

span.label: unified conscious field
span.quote: Here the aim is not to find the NCC for this or that conscious experience but to find out how the brain creates the unified conscious field in the first place

span.label: binocular rivalry
span.quote: In binocular rivalry, one stimulus (a picture of a face, say) is presented to one eye and another (a picture of a house) to the other eye of a conscious subject

span.label: NCC - FOR CONTENT CONSCIOUSNESS: the minimally sufficient neural conditions for a specific, mostly representational content being conscious rather than not being conscious
span.quote: the minimally sufficient neural conditions for a specific (mostly representational) content being conscious rather than not being conscious

span.label: NCC - FOR STATES OF CONSCIOUSNESS: the minimally sufficient conditions for a creature being in an overall conscious state rather than an overall unconscious state - a different contrast, and the paper's whole argument is that the two cannot stand in for each other
span.quote: NCC for states of consciousness : the minimally sufficient conditions for a creature’s being in an overall conscious state rather than an overall unconscious state

span.label: state consciousness - A TERM WHOSE SENSE THE AUTHOR CANNOT STATE SUCCINCTLY, and he gives that failure as the core motivation for writing the paper
span.quote: It is, however, difficult to express succinctly the sense in which ‘state consciousness’ should then be used – a fact which is a core motivation for writing this paper

span.label: the field's vocabulary - DECLARED NON-UNIFORM by the author, who then proceeds on the clustering of studies rather than on the terms
span.quote: The terminology in this area is unfortunately not uniform

span.label: extends → Searle (2005) on the content-based NCC approach
span.quote: Searle is right that the content NCC is irrelevant to consciousness, but – crucially – only when the target is the correlate of a content’s being conscious.

span.label: contradicts → Searle (2005) on adopting the state-based approach instead
span.quote: But, contra Searle, this is not what I shall advocate here.

span.label: unified conscious field —same-as→ state consciousness
span.quote: notice that Searle uses the term ‘‘unified conscious field” as a cognate term for state of consciousness

span.label: content consciousness —operationalised-as→ binocular rivalry
span.quote: Binocular rivalry is used in paradigm studies in consciousness science since the stimuli are held constant and so brain activity that correlates with reported perceptual shifts is likely to reveal the neural substrate of consciousness

span.label: Because content-based NCC studies hold the subject's overall conscious state fixed rather than manipulating it, that presupposed conscious state remains an uncontrolled potential cause of the content's being conscious, i.e. a confound.
span.quote: this shows that presupposing conscious states at least potentially introduces a confounding factor in the standard content-based NCC approach.

span.label: What the content-based approach can legitimately identify is the neural correlate of a content being selected for conscious presentation rather than not selected, which is a different target from a content's being conscious.
span.quote: The target seems to be to find the neural correlate of a content’s being selected for conscious presentation, rather than not selected, on the background assumption that the creature is already in an overall conscious state.

span.label: The same experimental method would serve researchers who care only about explicit representation and are agnostic about whether their subjects are conscious, so the method is not specifically directed at consciousness at all.
span.quote: They can be completely neutral about whether the creature is in fact in an overall conscious state or not and yet gain very fruitful results using this method.

span.label: In state-based studies there is a trade-off: the more carefully conscious content is matched across conditions, the weaker the grounds for believing the two conditions still differ in being conscious versus unconscious rather than being two conscious conditions.
span.quote: The lesson is that the better content is matched across conditions, the less certain we become that the conditions contrast the unconscious state with the conscious state rather than merely contrasting conscious states with conscious states.

span.label: Taking sustained, instruction-locked brain responses as evidence of consciousness makes voluntary control the criterion of consciousness, which substitutes volition for phenomenality and so changes the explanatory target.
span.quote: Now the mark of consciousness is voluntary control rather than what philosophers refer to as phenomenality (e.g., what it is like to experience pain or imagine tennis or to be conscious at all).

span.label: The alternative route of inferring state consciousness from the presence of a content NCC also fails, because the content-based approach already assumes the subject is in a conscious state and therefore cannot independently establish it.
span.quote: Section 3 showed that the content-based approach presupposes that the subjects in question are already in an overall conscious state and it therefore follows that it cannot be used to establish independently whether a subject is in fact conscious.

span.label: The paper concludes that neither the content-based nor the state-based paradigm, pursued on its own, can deliver the neural correlates of consciousness.
span.quote: It seems then that neither the content- nor the state-based approach taken in isolation from one another will help us discover the NCC.

span.label: The remedy proposed is not to conjoin the two approaches' results but to build a new paradigm that targets the causal, mechanistic interplay between content processing and overall conscious state across contents and across conscious and unconscious state types.
span.quote: Rather than merely conjoining the approaches, it may be that they must be integrated in a new type of experimental approach that targets the presumably causal, mechanistic interplay (cf. Bechtel 2007 ) between content processing and overall conscious state across different contents and across different types of conscious and unconscious states.

span.label: NCC for content consciousness
span.quote: NCC for content consciousness : the minimally sufficient neural conditions for a specific (mostly representational) content being conscious rather than not being conscious.

span.label: NCC for states of consciousness
span.quote: NCC for states of consciousness : the minimally sufficient conditions for a creature’s being in an overall conscious state rather than an overall unconscious state.

span.label: state-based study (operational criterion)
span.quote: As defined here, a study counts as state-based if it is directed at the contrast between being conscious rather than being unconscious.

span.label: total NCC
span.quote: It is natural to think of the state NCC plus the (union of) content NCCs as the total NCC.

span.label: neural correlates of volition (NCV)
span.quote: Finding the neural correlates of volition, the NC V, is a valid and important but different project from finding the NCC.

p.note: The full text of this article is not redistributable, so it is not included here. Every tag above carries the exact sentence it was made from, quoted under fair quotation. The article itself is at https://doi.org/10.1016/j.concog.2009.02.006.
